title: Come Turn With Me
tags: Whimsical European folk-pop and cinematic folk dance at a brisk 124 BPM. Open with gentle acoustic guitar, soft fiddle and wooden flute; bring in an expressive female lead, then gradually add accordion, mandolin, upright bass, hammered dulcimer and hand percussion. Keep verses light and intimate, build pre-choruses with claps and quiet backing voices, then lift into catchy choruses with a small mixed folk ensemble singing natural unison and simple harmonies. Add a communal call-and-response sing-along, an energetic fiddle-and-accordion dance exchange, a softer guitar-and-fiddle bridge with hummed backing voices, and a joyous full-ensemble final chorus. Organic acoustic arrangement, warm room ambience, lively hand claps and bodhrán, spontaneous human ensemble character, playful romantic storytelling, cheerful fairytale adventure, minimal electronic processing, concise fiddle-and-accordion ending.
prompt:
[Intro]
By the old stone well, where the market bells ring
You smiled as you tucked a blue ribbon in

[Verse 1]
You came with a basket of pears from the hill
And mud on your boots from the road by the mill
I offered my hand and you offered a grin
Then spun me so fast that my bonnet gave in

[Pre-Chorus]
The baker came laughing, the neighbors drew near
The fiddler struck up and the whole square could hear

[Chorus]
Come turn with me, my dear, come turn with me
Round by the fountain and under the tree
One step for the promise, two steps for the day
Come turn with me till the clouds roll away

[Folk Sing-Along]
Turn, turn, around we go
Hand in hand through the clover row
Turn, turn, bright as the day
Laugh with me and dance away

[Verse 2]
You traded your pears for a warm honey cake
I saved you the piece with the sugared heart shape
Your cousin kept time on an old wooden pail
While your aunt led the dance with a scarf for a veil

[Pre-Chorus]
The lanterns were lit and the fiddles rang clear
You leaned in and told me, “Stay close, my dear”

[Chorus]
Come turn with me, my dear, come turn with me
Round by the fountain and under the tree
One step for the promise, two steps for the day
Come turn with me till the clouds roll away

[Instrumental Dance Break]
[Fiddle and accordion trade lively melodies; ensemble calls and claps]

[Bridge]
When the last little lantern grows gentle and low
I’ll walk you back home past the bend in the road
And if you say yes when the morning birds sing
I’ll bring you blue ribbon and pears from the spring

[Final Chorus]
Come turn with me, my dear, come turn with me
Round by the fountain and under the tree
One step for the promise, two steps for the day
Come turn with me till the clouds roll away
Come turn with me, the whole village sings
Round by the fountain as morning bells ring
One step for the promise, two steps for the day
Come turn with me, come turn, come away

[Outro]
Turn, turn, around we go
Hand in hand through the clover row
Come turn with me, my dear
Come turn with me

title: The Hidden Kingdom
tags: Cinematic fantasy folk-pop, lilting 6/8 pulse, hammered dulcimer and harp arpeggios over warm strings, airy woodwinds, frame drums building into broad orchestral percussion for the final chorus. Clear expressive female lead with intimate verses and soaring, layered chorus; detailed natural reverb, wide strings, polished soundtrack mix.
prompt:
[Verse 1]
At the edge of the winter wood
Where the old stones drink the rain
I found a map beneath the roots
And heard it speak my name
A silver moth upon my sleeve
Turned east into the blue
So I took the road the ravens keep
And followed it to you

[Pre-Chorus]
Past the river, past the thorn
Past the tower split in two
There’s a door the dawn has sworn
Will open only true

[Chorus]
Carry me over the mountains of glass
Through the wild where the lost years sleep
I will bring back the fire they buried at last
I will wake what the deep hills keep
If the whole sky breaks, if the old bells call
I will stand where the brave hearts go
With your hand in mine, we can answer it all
And the hidden kingdom will know

[Verse 2]
In a hall of roots and amber light
A queen in leaves stood still
She wore the moon like a circlet bright
And held the storm at will
She said, “The crown is not your prize
Nor the blade your heart must claim
Choose the life that you would save
And speak its living name”

[Pre-Chorus]
Then I thought of every door
That I’d left unlatched behind
And the small, unguarded things
That make a kingdom kind

[Chorus]
Carry me over the mountains of glass
Through the wild where the lost years sleep
I will bring back the fire they buried at last
I will wake what the deep hills keep
If the whole sky breaks, if the old bells call
I will stand where the brave hearts go
With your hand in mine, we can answer it all
And the hidden kingdom will know

[Bridge]
I spoke your name; the roots let go
The frozen wells began to run
The queen laid down her crown of snow
And turned her face toward the sun
No throne can hold what love sets free
No spell can bind a heart that chooses
The dawn came walking through the trees
And every road became ours to use

[Final Chorus]
Carry us over the mountains of glass
Through the wild where the lost years sleep
We have brought back the fire they buried at last
We have woken what the deep hills keep
Let the whole sky break, let the old bells call
We are more than the fear we know
With your hand in mine, we can answer it all
And the hidden kingdom will grow

[Outro]
At the edge of the waking wood
Where the bright streams run anew
I kept the map beneath my coat
And every road led back to you

title: Feast Beneath the Harvest Moon
tags: Whimsical European folk-pop dance, 125 BPM, buoyant lilting dance pulse with an energetic but graceful village-festival feel. Entirely organic acoustic ensemble: fiddle, accordion, mandolin, acoustic guitar, wooden flute, hammered dulcimer, upright bass, tambourine, bodhrán, and hand claps; natural room ambience and live ensemble dynamics, minimal processing. Arrange distinct sections: intimate female solo over gentle guitar, fiddle, and soft flute; then a rustic mixed-gender village ensemble singing alone in natural unison and simple harmonies with claps and light percussion; then a clearly forward female lead joined by communal ensemble responses and harmonies over the full band; return to a softer female solo with guitar and fiddle; give the folk ensemble a lively sing-along over accordion, fiddle, mandolin, and claps; finish with everyone together in a joyful full-band celebration, followed by one gentle female phrase alone, a short cheerful ensemble answer, and a fiddle-and-accordion finish. Keep the female lead distinct in the joined passages, and use no classical, operatic, or gospel choir.
prompt:
[Verse 1 — Female Solo]
You tied a blue ribbon round the gate,
And left your basket by the pear-tree shade.
I came with rain still caught upon my sleeve,
You laughed and asked me if I’d stay till eve.

[Chorus — Folk Ensemble Solo]
Turn the mill-wheel, stamp the ground,
Pass the cider, gather round.
Hey, little sparrow, carry the tune,
We’ll make a feast beneath the harvest moon.

[Verse 2 — Female Lead and Folk Ensemble]
I take your hand where the old stones shine,
Your neighbors clap and fall in line.
You sing the words I nearly knew,
And every face is singing too.

[Chorus — Female Lead and Folk Ensemble]
Turn the mill-wheel, stamp the ground,
Pass the cider, gather round.
Hey, little sparrow, carry the tune,
We’ll make a feast beneath the harvest moon.

[Verse 3 — Female Solo]
The lanterns sway above the square,
A sprig of rosemary in your hair.
You tell me tomorrow can wait its turn,
While apple cakes and kindling burn.

[Chorus — Folk Ensemble Solo]
Turn the mill-wheel, stamp the ground,
Pass the cider, gather round.
Hey, little sparrow, carry the tune,
We’ll make a feast beneath the harvest moon.

[Final Chorus — Female Lead and Folk Ensemble]
Turn the mill-wheel, stamp the ground,
Pass the cider, gather round.
Hey, little sparrow, carry the tune,
We’ll make a feast beneath the harvest moon.
You and I, and the whole town too,
Keep this merry circle turning through.

[Ending — Female Solo]
Stay till the last pear blossom falls.

[Folk Ensemble Answer]
Hey, little sparrow, sing to us all!

[Instrumental Outro: fiddle and accordion]
